## Objective
- Build a complete, playable “Steam × Windows” virtual-desktop game for PC and mobile, with desktop apps, a Steam-like launcher, virtual files, and original mini-games.

## Requirements
- Windows-inspired desktop with wallpaper, Steam, Blender, Google, and File Explorer apps; Steam should be a separate desktop app.
- Steam should offer many free games, with an install-to-virtual-C-drive confirmation before launch and options to cancel or return to Steam.
- Include original playable experiences inspired by battle royale, horror survival, block building, platformers, and other genres; support mobile controls.
- Google should be a safe simulated search experience that blocks inappropriate searches with a 404-style page, and can launch browser mini-games.
- File Manager should support virtual files, folders, copy/paste, rename, delete, and extracting an archive; Blender-inspired app should allow basic shape and scale editing.
- User asked for realistic app iconography and sound effects; the current implementation does not yet include sound effects.

## Decisions
- Implemented an original, self-contained browser game inspired by the requested apps and genres rather than reproducing branded commercial games or real search results.
- Used locally generated demo search results and original Canvas mini-games; virtual files remain in browser localStorage and are not written to the real device.
- Used a CSS mountain landscape wallpaper rather than a copyrighted Windows wallpaper.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a responsive virtual Windows-style desktop, Start menu, taskbar, wallpaper, and app windows.
- Implemented Steam store/library with 16 original game listings, category filters, search, install confirmation, and launch flow.
- Implemented playable original mini-games: Skyfall Royale, Midnight at Freddy’s-inspired night survival, Blocklands, platformer variants, and Pixel Painter; added keyboard/touch controls.
- Implemented safe simulated Google search, Blender-inspired shape/scale workspace, and virtual File Explorer features.
- `node --check app.js` succeeded.

- Browser QA is not yet complete; a local development server was started and Playwright CLI availability confirmed.

1. Open `http://localhost:3002` with Playwright, test desktop/mobile layout and key app/game interactions, save a small JPEG screenshot and inspect the latest one.

3. Consider adding sound effects and polishing any rough features found during testing.
4. Report assumptions and verification results to the user.

- `index.html`: desktop DOM, taskbar, Start menu, and app icon entry points.
- `styles.css`: desktop visuals, app windows, responsive/mobile layout, and game styling.
- `app.js`: app behavior, Steam catalog, install flow, browser/files/Blender, and mini-game logic.

## Important Context
- Local server command was `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The work has not been committed or pushed.
- User asked for a complete playable game and explicitly said not to ask clarifying questions.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable “Steam × Windows” virtual-desktop game for PC and mobile, with desktop apps, virtual files, and original mini-games.

## Requirements
- Include separate Steam, Blender, Google, and File Explorer apps, plus wallpaper, app icons, and a Windows-inspired desktop.
- Steam should offer many free games, ask before installing to a virtual C: drive, and allow cancel or return to Steam.
- Include playable original games inspired by battle royale, horror survival, block building, platformers, and other genres, with mobile controls.
- Google should simulate safe search, show a 404-style page for inappropriate searches, and launch browser mini-games.
- File Explorer should support virtual files and folders, copy/paste, rename, delete, and archive extraction.
- Blender-inspired app should support basic shape and scale editing.
- User also requested realistic app iconography and button sound effects; sound effects remain unimplemented.

## Decisions
- Built an original, self-contained browser game inspired by the requested apps and genres rather than reproducing branded commercial games or real search results.
- Search results are local demo content; virtual files are stored in browser localStorage and are not written to the real device.
- Used a CSS mountain landscape wallpaper rather than a copyrighted Windows wallpaper.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive virtual Windows-style desktop, Start menu, taskbar, wallpaper, windows, and app icons.
- Implemented Steam store/library with 16 original game listings, category filters, search, install confirmation, and launch flow.
- Added Canvas mini-games, including Skyfall Royale, night survival, Blocklands, platformer variants, and Pixel Painter, with touch controls.
- Implemented simulated safe Google search, Blender-inspired shape/scale workspace, and virtual File Explorer features.
- Started local server at `http://localhost:3002`; server returned HTTP 200.
- `node --check app.js` completed without errors before the latest edits.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable “Steam × Windows” virtual-desktop game for PC and mobile, with desktop apps, virtual files, and original mini-games.

## Requirements
- Include separate Steam, Blender, Google, and File Explorer apps, plus wallpaper, app icons, and a Windows-inspired desktop.
- Steam should offer many free games, ask before installing to a virtual C: drive, and allow cancel or return to Steam.
- Include playable original games inspired by battle royale, horror survival, block building, platformers, and other genres, with mobile controls.
- Google should simulate safe search, show a 404-style page for inappropriate searches, and launch browser mini-games.
- File Explorer should support virtual files and folders, copy/paste, rename, delete, and archive extraction.
- Blender-inspired app should support basic shape and scale editing.
- User also requested realistic app iconography and button sound effects; sound effects remain unimplemented.

## Decisions
- Built an original, self-contained browser game inspired by the requested apps and genres rather than reproducing branded commercial games or real search results.
- Search results are local demo content; virtual files are stored in browser localStorage and are not written to the real device.
- Used a CSS mountain landscape wallpaper rather than a copyrighted Windows wallpaper.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive virtual Windows-style desktop, Start menu, taskbar, wallpaper, windows, and app icons.
- Implemented Steam store/library with 16 original game listings, category filters, search, install confirmation, and launch flow.
- Added Canvas mini-games, including Skyfall Royale, night survival, Blocklands, platformer variants, and Pixel Painter, with touch controls.
- Implemented simulated safe Google search, Blender-inspired shape/scale workspace, and virtual File Explorer features.

- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002` and returned HTTP 200.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable “Steam × Windows” virtual-desktop game for PC and mobile, with desktop apps, virtual files, and original mini-games.

## Requirements
- Include separate Steam, Blender, Google, and File Explorer apps, plus wallpaper, app icons, and a Windows-inspired desktop.
- Steam should offer free games, ask before installing to a virtual C: drive, and allow cancel or return to Steam.
- Include playable original games inspired by battle royale, horror survival, block building, platformers, and other genres, with mobile controls.
- Google should simulate safe search, show a 404-style page for inappropriate searches, and launch browser mini-games.
- File Explorer should support virtual files and folders, copy/paste, rename, delete, and archive extraction.
- Blender-inspired app should support basic shape and scale editing.
- Add realistic app iconography and button sound effects.

## Decisions
- Built an original, self-contained browser game inspired by the requested apps and genres rather than reproducing branded commercial games or real search results.
- Search results are local demo content; virtual files are stored in browser localStorage and are not written to the real device.
- Used a CSS mountain landscape wallpaper rather than a copyrighted Windows wallpaper.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive virtual Windows-style desktop, Start menu, taskbar, wallpaper, windows, and app icons.
- Implemented Steam store/library with 16 original game listings, category filters, search, install confirmation, and launch flow.
- Added Canvas mini-games, including Skyfall Royale, night survival, Blocklands, platformer variants, and Pixel Painter, with touch controls.
- Implemented simulated safe Google search, Blender-inspired shape/scale workspace, and virtual File Explorer features.
- Verified `node --check app.js`; browser tests passed for Steam installation and launch, safe search blocking and browser game launch, ZIP extraction, and Blender shape/scale/save.
- Tested responsive layout at 390×844; game window and mobile controls fit in viewport without document overflow. Fixed mobile window vertical positioning in `styles.css`.
- Added an empty favicon data URL in `index.html`; browser console reported no errors or warnings after reload.
- Local server returned HTTP 200 at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Added a sound-effects toggle button (`#soundToggle`) to the taskbar in `index.html`.

- Implement sound effects and wire the taskbar sound toggle.
- Continue mobile game interaction QA; a synthetic pointer event did not immediately change the displayed score.

1. Implement button sound effects and connect `#soundToggle` to enable/disable them.
2. Continue browser QA for mobile game interactions and address any rough edges.
3. Re-run `node --check app.js` and browser console checks after changes.
4. Report verification results and note that changes remain uncommitted.

- `index.html`: desktop DOM, taskbar, Start menu, and desktop app entry points.
- `styles.css`: desktop visuals, app windows, responsive/mobile layout, and game styling.
- `app.js`: app behavior, Steam catalog, install flow, browser/files/Blender, and mini-game logic.

- Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript with no framework.
